metadata.title: Detect Repository
metadata.purposeAndUsage: Auto-detect the Azure DevOps repository ID from the git remote URL and find the PR linked to the work item. One-time setup step that provides repository context for all subsequent PR-related operations.

output.description: Repository ID, name, project, and linked PR ID stored in memory

prerequisites: workItemId parameter available from process parameters
Git remote configured with Azure DevOps URL
specificActions: Follow the substeps below in sequence
Workflow: parse git remote → call MCP for repo ID → find linked PR → store in memory
Support both SSH and HTTPS remote URL formats
If git remote parsing fails, report the error clearly and stop
To find the PR: first try fetching the work item relations to find a PR link, then fall back to searching PRs by source branch
tools: mcp__azuredevops__repo_repository - Get repository details by name
mcp__azuredevops__wit_work_item - Fetch work item to find PR link in relations
mcp__azuredevops__repo_pull_request - Search for PRs if no direct link found
bestPractices: Always extract project and repo name from the remote URL — do not hardcode
Log the detected remote URL format (SSH vs HTTPS) for traceability
When searching for linked PRs, check work item relations first (faster than searching all PRs)
If multiple PRs are linked, use the most recent active one
Store the full repository object in memory for downstream steps

substeps.name: Parse Git Remote URL
substeps.description: Extract project and repository name from git remote
actions: Run `git remote get-url origin` to get the remote URL
Parse the URL to extract organization, project, and repository name
SSH pattern: git@ssh.dev.azure.com:v3/{org}/{project}/{repo}
HTTPS pattern: https://dev.azure.com/{org}/{project}/_git/{repo}
If parsing fails: report error and STOP
Log: 'Detected remote: {format} — project={project}, repo={repo}'

substeps.name: Fetch Repository ID via MCP
substeps.description: Call Azure DevOps MCP to get the repository details
actions: Call mcp__azuredevops__repo_repository with project and repositoryNameOrId from parsed URL
Extract the repository `id` field from the response
If the call fails: report error and STOP
Log: 'Repository ID: {id}'

substeps.name: Find Linked Pull Request
substeps.description: Find the PR associated with the work item
actions: Call mcp__azuredevops__wit_work_item with project and workItemId, expand='all'
Search relations array for a PR link (relation type contains 'Pull Request' or URL contains '/_apis/git/repositories/')
If PR link found: extract PR ID from the relation URL
If no PR link in relations: fall back to searching PRs by querying mcp__azuredevops__repo_pull_request for active PRs in the repository, filter by work item link
If no PR found at all: log warning — the PR may not exist yet, store pullRequestId as null
Log: 'Found PR #{pullRequestId}' or 'No PR linked to work item {workItemId}'

substeps.name: Store Results in Memory
substeps.description: Write repository and PR details to memory
actions: Write to memory: repository.id, repository.name, repository.project, pullRequestId
If pullRequestId is null, note this explicitly for downstream steps to handle

substeps.name: End-Step: Compliance Check
substeps.description: Verify principles were followed in this step
actions: Verify: Was log.json updated for any user interactions?
Verify: Were mandatory actions confirmed with output?
Verify: Repository ID was successfully extracted
Output: 'Step completed in compliance with operating principles'

flow.description: Linear flow: Parse git remote URL → Call MCP for repository ID → Find linked PR via work item relations or PR search → Store in memory → Compliance check

fields: Information Produced: repository.id, repository.name, repository.project, pullRequestId
Decisions Made: Remote URL format detection (SSH vs HTTPS), PR discovery method (relation link vs search)
Notes: Any warnings about missing PR link
